17-13-0303-C(1) Type i Narrative & Plans — 1921 West Chicago Avenue, Chicago, IL
Proposed Zoning: B3-3 Community Shopping District
Lot Area: Approximately 2,952 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to redevelop the subject property with a new
four-story mixed-use building containing one (1) retail space on the first
floor, containing approximately 850 sq. ft. of floor area, and three (3)
residential dwelling units on the floors above. The new building will
measure approximately 44 ft.-11 in. in height. The subject property is a
Transit Served Location and will be supported by three (3) off-street garage
parking spaces. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-0303-D optional Administrative
Adjustment and Variation and pursuant to Secs. 17-13-1003-EE and 17-13-
1101-B of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the Applicant is seeking to
increase the residential off-street parking ratio from 66% (2 parking spaces)
to 100% (3 parking spaces), reduce the rear setback for floors containing
residential units from 30 feet to 1 ft.-6 in., and is seeking all zoning relief,
as needed and as allowed by the Chicago Zoning Code, for the attached
plans.

(A) _ The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 7,434.6 square feet (2.52 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 984 square feet per D.U.
(3 residential units)

© The amount of off-street parking: 3 parking spaces total

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location based on its
proximity to Chicago CTA bus line corridor. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-EE, the
Applicant is seeking to increase the off-street parking ratio from 66% (2 parking
spaces) to 100% (3 parking spaces).

(D) Setbacks:
a. Front Setback: zero
b. Side Setbacks:
East Side: 6 inches
West Side: 3 feet
c. *Rear Setback: 1 feet-6 inches.

*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1101-B, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the rear setback
for floors containing residential units from 30 feet to 1 ft.-6 in.

(E) Building Height: 44 ft.-11 in. in height

Final for Publication

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1, The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 220 linear feet of the Western CTA bus line
corridor. The proposed mixed-use building containing one (1) retail/commercial space on
the first floor and three (3) residential units above will be supported by three (3) off-street
parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to permit an
increase in the residential off-sireet parking ratio from 66% (2 parking spaces) to 100% (3
parking spaces).

2. The Applicant’s building design complies with the main building door and entryway design
standards provided by Sec. 17-4-0504 because the main residential entrance of the
proposed building at 1921 West Chicago Avenue fronts along West Chicago Avenue and
the proposed front setback is zero. Furthermore, the entrance widths do not exceed 12 ft.,
the entrance depths do not exceed the entrance width, the entrances are not more than two-
stories in height, and the proposed building elevations comply with the window
transparency requirements.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines “transit friendly development” as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
mixed-use building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the Western Avenue CTA bus line corridor. The Applicant believes the
redevelopment of an underutilized lot will improve the subject area for residents and other
commuters traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed mixed-use building will contain approximately 850 sq. ft. of
retail/commercial space on the first floor and three (3) residential units above. The
proposed building will be supported by three (3) off-street parking spaces. The Applicant
is seeking administrative approval to permit the off-street parking increase for the
residential units pursuant to the TOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed mixed-use building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace a two-story
residence with a new mixed-use building, which will provide additional residential housing
thereby meeting market demand. Based on the subject property’s proximity to a designated
CTA bus line corridor (Western Avenue bus route #66), the Applicant believes the project
provides transit options and otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and
Management Plan rules promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an
area in need.
